svg.title: Layered (N-Tier)
svg.desc: Layered (N-Tier). Presentation, business and data layers; each layer only calls the one directly below it. Step 1, One job, closed layers: Place order travels down: each layer does one job and calls only the layer directly below it. Step 2, Change one layer: New database: only Data access changes. JSON API: only Presentation. Business is tested on a fake. Step 3, Layers are not tiers: Layers organise code, tiers are where it runs: three tiers scale and secure apart but add hops. Step 4, Three traps: Traps: sinkhole reads, open layers that skip Business, and one new field that touches every layer.

g.text: Place order travels down: each layer does one job and calls only the layer directly below it.
New database: only Data access changes. JSON API: only Presentation. Business is tested on a fake.
Layers organise code, tiers are where it runs: three tiers scale and secure apart but add hops.
Traps: sinkhole reads, open layers that skip Business, and one new field that touches every layer.
CODE · imports go one layer down; no skipping
CODE · the same code in both deployments
CODE · where the traps show up
PLACE ORDER · one job per layer
only the Data access code changes
app tier admits web tier only
db tier admits app tier only
A simple read crosses every layer and
none of them does any work: latency
Business is opened so reads can skip it.
One new field touches every layer: the
split is by technical role, not feature.
→ core not tied to the DB (hexagonal)
calls from above must go through this layer
